content: It is crucial to take this medication exactly as directed on the product packaging. Do not skip any doses. If you experience stomach upset or nausea, taking the medication after your evening meal or at bedtime may help. Alternatively, you can choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. Continue taking one tablet every day without interruption. Once you finish the last tablet in your current pack, start a new pack the following day. Your menstrual periods may become irregular, including being early or late, shorter or longer, heavier or lighter than usual. Spotting between periods may also occur. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on switching from other forms of hormonal birth control, such as patches or other birth control pills, to this product. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, increased appetite, stomach cramping or bloating, dizziness, or headache. Vaginal spotting or irregular periods may occur, especially during the first few months of use. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This medication does not protect against sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) such as HIV, hepatitis B, gonorrhea, or syphilis. To reduce the risk of infection, always use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity. Before taking norgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as tartrazine, which can cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication must not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. A small amount of this medication may pass into breast milk, but it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Certain drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new medication and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, potentially causing false test results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. If you miss a dose, refer to the product package for instructions. You may need to use backup birth control, such as condoms or spermicide, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
